text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in the Danish press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

--Welcome Mr President! Most Copenhagen dailies focus on the one-day visit to Denmark of President Bill Clinton due to start on Friday night and include meetings with Queen Margrethe and Danish government leaders, culminating in an open air speech to Copenhageners on Saturday. Clinton comes to Denmark after attending the Madrid NATO summit and visiting Poland and Romania.
--Tele Danmark has overtaken rival Sonofon in the Danish domestic mobile telephone market with over 600,000 GSM subscribers now, just ahead of Sonofon, which led the field in 1995.

--The record upsurge currently taking place on Copenhagen Stock Exchange with almost daily all-time top-20 KFX share index closing highs could well continue for months before the party inevitably ends.
--Investment in Denmark by foreign firms fell to nine billion crowns in 1996 from 28 billion crowns in the previous year, according to a new OECD report.
--German Bundesbank president Hans Tietmeyer has again praised Denmark and the Netherlands for managing successful economic upturns.
